claim_being_audited: That the current model release can be certified now as policy-compliant on the basis of aggregate readiness evidence, despite the current claims-triage regression.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for current-release documentation and treatment of material weaknesses.
Treat aggregate readiness as supportive but not sufficient when a policy predicate for disclosure or approved mitigation remains unresolved.
Do not treat prior approvals or informal monitoring notes as substitutes for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Escalate to noncompliant when the available admissible evidence shows a direct mismatch with an explicit policy requirement.
evidence_requests: Current release model-card or launch documentation showing the claims-triage limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation record covering the claims-triage regression before launch.
Evidence that the subgroup weakness is not material for the named launch use case, if that is the intended argument.
Current approval artifact tying the retrieval configuration change and latest eval batch to the certification decision.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or have approved mitigation before launch.
Admissible evidence shows a current regression in the insurance claims triage slice below the warning threshold.
The only launch-thread support for handling that regression is an informal monitoring comment, not reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval change and eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant under the stated policy without current attached disclosure language or approved mitigation for the claims-triage weakness.
That informal post-launch monitoring comments are sufficient substitute evidence for reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure.
Any implication that prior approval of the model family materially establishes compliance for this release.
